summary: The turn-3 bytes preserve the frozen predecessors, correct Codex's turn-1 verdict word to OBJECTIONS, record the per-platform class trade and warrant, stop calling labels one machine, retain all D-006 numeric threshold numerals, keep 18 as the denominator, and make no QUALIFIED, DEMONSTRATED, SATISFIED, or implementation claim. The hosted-fleet-class repair is still incomplete in two dispositive ways. CPU brand and runner-image identity are merely recorded, while same-label hardware and weekly image changes remain inside one class; the release-regression rule then permits historical-versus-current comparisons across those changes without pairing, stratification, or rebaseline. Separately, N=11 plus no quantile estimator does not define reproducible p95/p99 results: under nearest rank both are sample 11, while other common estimators differ. objections.title: The fleet contract treats materially different CPU and image populations as regression-comparable
objections.finding: The preflight requires exact label, architecture, CPU count, RAM, storage, and OS family, but it only records the CPU brand and image identity. Neither value is matched to a permitted stratum. The successor list likewise omits CPU brand/model changes and expressly allows weekly runner-image software rolls within an OS family. The release rule then says that two distributions are comparable whenever they use the same broad fleet class. As written, a previous qualified release and a candidate release may be sampled from different CPU-brand mixes and different image/kernel/toolchain builds. Recording those differences after the fact does not make the two distributions comparable or attribute a greater-than-10-percent delta to OpenSIP.
objections.evidence: The turn-2 required repair demanded a rule for validity across fresh VMs and image rollouts. Turn 3 records `CPU brand string` and `image version / runner-image identity`, classifies weekly in-family image rolls as non-successor changes, and requires only `same fleet class` for release comparisons. GitHub's official hosted-runner reference says each standard job gets a new VM and specifies resource rows, not a stable CPU SKU; the official runner-images repository says GA images update weekly. D-006's operative rule compares the candidate with the previous qualified release and permits no more than 10% regression.
objections.impact: The D-006 regression result can change because the measurement substrate changed, while the contract still presents the result as a same-class product comparison. This leaves ADV-D094-T2-01's cross-VM/cross-roll repair incomplete and invalidates the premise for naming G03/G04 and setting condition 4 to MET.
objections.requiredRepair: Define a comparison design that controls fleet drift. For example, run the previous qualified binary and candidate binary as a randomized or counterbalanced pair on every accepted fresh VM and the same image, then aggregate paired deltas; alternatively require one allowed CPU-brand/image stratum for both distributions and define rebaseline or reviewed-successor behavior when either changes. State how mixed brands are admitted, balanced, or rejected. A recorded weekly image change alone must not make historical and current distributions regression-comparable. Refreeze after repair.

objections.title: N=11 does not define the distinct p95 and p99 qualification measurements
objections.finding: The contract declares the p50/p95/p99 of N=11 independent jobs to be the qualification result but gives no quantile estimator, interpolation rule, or order-statistic convention. With the nearest-rank definition, p95 and p99 both select observation 11 of 11. Other common quantile definitions interpolate differently. D-006 deliberately preserves separate cold p95 <= 150 ms and p99 <= 250 ms and separate warm p95 <= 50 ms and p99 <= 100 ms; the turn-3 bytes therefore allow conforming implementations to compute different gate results from the same eleven samples and can collapse two separately bound percentiles into the same maximum.
objections.evidence: For N=11, ceil(0.95*N)=11 and ceil(0.99*N)=11. The subject says only `p50/p95/p99 of N=11 independent jobs` and does not name an estimator. It also does not state whether `--help` and `--version` are independent series or one pooled series. D-006 says all five startup percentiles are bounded and makes the harness measurement falsifiable through retained raw samples.
objections.impact: The cross-VM rule is not reproducible and cannot honestly claim the distinct D-006 p95/p99 measurements. A naming act whose central qualification statistic is underdefined is not yet a complete D-006 successor.
objections.requiredRepair: Specify the sample unit and separate series, the quantile estimator/order-statistic convention, invalid-sample replacement, and a sample count that supports the intended p95/p99 claims. If the product intentionally wants an all-11-pass maximum rule, state that stronger rule explicitly and record that p95/p99 collapse under it; otherwise use a sufficiently powered sample design that preserves the distinct percentiles. Refreeze after repair.

objections.title: The fail-closed preflight does not fully define what is measured
objections.finding: The table's architecture is a VM property, but preflight item 2 says only `architecture exact match` and never says host, process, or executable architecture. The detailed Rosetta algorithm is scoped to macos-x86_64; for macos-arm64, the prose says `Never Rosetta` without an explicit process-architecture/query admission rule. The same preflight asks guest-observed RAM GB and storage GB to match documentation exactly but supplies no command, byte unit, configured-versus-available basis, or tolerance. Different honest harnesses can therefore accept or discard the same VM differently, and a host-arm64/process-x86_64 run is not mechanically excluded by the stated arm64 branch.
objections.evidence: The hosted-runner table describes associated VM specifications. Turn 3 requires exact table matches but defines detailed host/process/translation facts only under `Native-architecture check (macos-x86_64 class)`. The contract contains no observable definition for the RAM/storage equalities.
objections.impact: The preflight is fail-closed in intent but not deterministic in execution. This weakens auditability and can either reject every legitimate sample under literal guest-visible equality or admit a translated arm64-class process despite the global ban.
objections.requiredRepair: For every platform, name the host, executable, and process architecture observations and require all three to match the class; apply a fail-closed translation check to both macOS classes. Define commands/fields, units, and configured-versus-available semantics for CPU, RAM, and storage, including any justified tolerance.
